title: The ten-minute monthly money review
description: Once a month, ten minutes, four questions. That is the whole system — and it catches almost every money problem while it is still small.

body.heading: The four questions
paragraphs: Sit down with your banking app and ask: what came in, what went out, what surprised me, and what changes next month? Ten honest minutes. No spreadsheets are required, though a notebook of the answers is surprisingly motivating over time.

The surprise question does most of the work. Money stress usually comes from surprises — the forgotten renewal, the creeping category — and a monthly review shrinks the maximum age of any surprise to thirty days.

body.heading: Check the standing machinery
paragraphs: Glance at the automatic parts of your money while you are there: savings transfers still running, subscriptions still wanted, bills still correct. Systems drift; a monthly glance is how you notice before drift becomes damage.
Also check progress on your current goal, however small. Seeing a pot grow by even a little, on paper, once a month, is the feedback loop that keeps habits alive.

body.heading: End with one action
paragraphs: Close the review by choosing exactly one action for the coming month: cancel one thing, raise one transfer by $5, re-quote one bill. One action, done, beats a page of intentions. Then close the app and get on with your life — the review is a servant, not a hobby.

Pick a fixed day for the review — payday works well, or the first of the month — and attach it to something you already do, like a particular coffee or commute. Habits anchored to existing routines rarely need motivation to survive.

takeaway: Ten minutes monthly: in, out, surprises, one change. Small problems caught early stay small, and goals stay visible.
